problem: A 'blocking' question with a default has no defined meaning, and its effects contradict the default it states. The default is shown to Sam but never applied, so inc-016 and inc-039 stay blocked for ever. N of TOTAL can never reach 100%, and the default's real consequence (a rejected atom and a dropped increment) never appears in section 2 as a call Sam can reverse. That is a gate dressed as a default, which feedback_headless_make_calls_dont_gate forbids. The house-rules question also defaults to A while recommending B, and gives no reason.
evidence: q-house-rules-source: class 'blocking', ifNobodyAnswers.option 'A', but option A's effect is {op: reject, target: req-046} while its consequence says the increment 'stays blocked'. q-dr1u-remainder: default B's effect is 'reject req-110', but the text says it 'stays blocked'. Sections 3.6 and 3.10 never say when a blocking question's default is applied, yet the 5.6 lint rule requires a default on every question that is not must-answer. q-house-rules-source has recommended 'B' and default 'A'.
fix: Keep two behaviours only. A must-answer question has ifNobodyAnswers.option null and blocks. Any other question has its default applied by `tim backlog rule --by default`, which writes a decision with status 'defaulted' and runs its effects. The report lists that decision in section 2 with 'To reverse', and the question stays in section 1 under 'Has a default in force'. Add lint rules: the default's effects must agree with its consequence text (checked by the QUESTION_CRITIC), and a default that differs from `recommended` needs a `defaultWhy`. Re-derive inc-016 and inc-039 as dropped or deferred under their defaults.

section: DESIGN 5.10, 9.2 S5, Q35; decisions-for-sam.md section 1; backlog.json sources
problem: The gate on conversational sources blocks Sam's own main channel (chat and voice), contradicts section 5.10, and can be bypassed by relabelling a source. Option A (quotes stay on this machine, a paraphrase goes to git) is the most conservative option that still accepts these sources, and raw/ is already gitignored for every kind. So having no default protects nothing and breaks R1's 'loose requirements from anywhere'. Because the gate keys on source kind, pasting the same chat as markdown bypasses it, which is what this programme did with its own brief. Rulings also already put Sam's conversational words into git.
evidence: DESIGN 5.10 says transcripts, chat and email are 'local by default (S5)'. DESIGN 9.2 and decisions-for-sam.md say 'no default … conversational sources stay off'. backlog.json registers sam-req (Sam's conversational brief) as kind 'markdown', retention 'tracked'. decisions[].words holds the ruler's words verbatim in tracked backlog.json (3.7, 5.8). feedback_question_is_not_a_ruling names only security, access control and data integrity as must-answer; Q35 widens that to legal and policy.
fix: Put option A in force now as the default. Keep a must-answer question only for 'may third parties' words enter git?' (option B). Base retention on the speaker, not the source kind. Add kind 'brief' for the requester's own instructions (tracked, stated, role requirement), and keep other people's utterances local whatever the container. Exempt decisions[].words explicitly as the ruler's own words. Unblock inc-031.

problem: The answer sheet lists question ids only, which breaks the design's own headline-first rule and its own lint rule. Sam fills it in away from the page and has to look up what 'A' means, which reopens the 'question 3 meant 17/18' ambiguity.
evidence: The 6.4 sheet contains only 'q-notification-list-scope:', 'q-commodity-code-grain:' and 'q-error-summary-title:', with no headline, options or default. Rule 6.1(3) says an id is never the only label, and `report --lint` fails 'an id shown without its headline'. The only sheet test is 'parses back to the same question ids'.
fix: Above each answer line, generate comment lines giving the headline, each lettered option in one line with its source count, the recommendation, and 'If nobody answers'. Run the same lint over the sheet as over the page. Add a renderer test that every sheet id comes with its headline and every option letter.

problem: Reversing a call the machine made is neither paste-ready nor batchable. Section 2 exists so Sam can overturn precedence picks, panel rulings, defaults and automatic combinations. Today each reversal needs an agent to work out the command, and none can go in a batch.
evidence: The skeleton says 'To reverse: rule conflict c-004 for Confluence.', which is a bare id with no command. Batch controls and the answer sheet cover questions[] only. Conflicts carry resolution.pick but no reversal effects, and combinations carry none. Holds in section 1(b), by contrast, print a runnable 'tim backlog state … release' command.
fix:
Give every section 2 entry a generated, paste-ready command, such as `tim backlog rule

--subject conflict:c-004 --choose --by sam --at --note …`, or `--subject combination: --split`, plus a batch checkbox. Add answer-sheet lines for reversals ('c-004: reverse ') and for holds ('inc-015: release '). Give conflicts and combinations predeclared reverseEffects. Add a renderer test that every section 2 entry carries a command that parses.

section: DESIGN 6.3 skeleton, section 1 'Has a default in force'
problem: Defaulted questions lose their four parts in the report. By design they are the most common class, so most questions reach Sam without options he can answer by letter. The 'If you choose otherwise' column is singular, so it cannot describe three options.
evidence: Rule 6.2 row 1 says every question has four parts. The skeleton's table has only Question, Default in force and If you choose otherwise: no 'in play', no lettered options, no counts. g-reports section 1.1 kept four columns even in the compact form.
fix: Render each defaulted question as a compact card: the headline, one line of 'In play', the lettered options with count and consequence, then 'In force: A'. Alternatively, add an Options column to the table. Add a renderer test that every question, whatever its class, shows all four parts.

problem: 'Ruled not a requirement' is decided by the author alone and never checked. It is the largest route by which a unit can drop out silently. A wrong or lazy author can pass P4 by dismissing units, and Sam sees only a count.
evidence: The coverage check (DESIGN line 825) passes a unit 'listed by its slice's author as not a requirement, with a reason'. The verifier's rubric (5.4) checks atoms only. The skeleton's P4 row shows '401 not requirements' of 1,104 units (36%) as a bare number. Section 9 shows notRaised[], which is a different list.
fix: The verify task must return a verdict on every dismissal: agree, or dispute with an added atom. P4 fails on any dismissal nobody verified. Report section 6 lists dismissals grouped by reason, each expanding to its units and quotes. Section 3 counts the dismissals that came from requirement-role sources.

problem: Links to material that was never fetched can disappear. Spreadsheets and slide decks, the usual loose sources in this organisation, have no source kind. The one real precedent lost its requirements catalogue this way, and this design would still pass it.
evidence: In 5.9, links the characteriser did not follow become units of kind 'pointer', but no rule forces them anywhere, and P1 and P4 accept them as 'not a requirement'. f-requirements-sources.md line 32 records that in the plants run the requirements catalogue was 'a SharePoint Excel workbook linked from the page and not fetched'. The kind enum has no spreadsheet or slides kind.
fix: Make P1 fail while any pointer unit on a requirement-role source is not one of: registered as a source, stated absent with a reason, or raised as a question (for example, 'The Confluence page links a requirements workbook we could not fetch. Can you export it?'). Add kinds 'spreadsheet' (xlsx and csv, cited by sheet, row and column) and 'slides' (pptx), each with a source-types file. Tell the characteriser to ask for an export when it meets a SharePoint or OneDrive link.

problem: The list of source kinds contradicts itself on prototypes and live services. The live-animals prototype and the Design Release parity corpora are the workspace's main requirement sources. Without a way to acquire and cite a prototype, no author can cite one as observed, and the role check refuses citations the design itself expects.
evidence: The 3.8 kind enum includes 'prototype'. The 5.10 acquisition table has no prototype row, and 5.9's source-types list has no prototype.md. The 3.12 role check says 'observed' needs 'a prototype, trace-corpus or live source', and 'live' is not a kind.
fix: Add a prototype row: a pinned repo plus rendered capture through parity's capture specs, token '<prototype>:<route>/<region>@<sha>', role requirement, 'observed' for rendered behaviour and 'stated' for copy. Add source-types/prototype.md. Either add a 'live-service' kind (a URL plus capture) or remove 'live' from the role check.

problem: The design's own six questions fail its own question checks (P8), and no QUESTION_CRITIC ever read them. These are the only questions Sam sees before the report increment (inc-025) exists. Several defects are exactly what the critic's rubric is meant to fail.
evidence: Checked with `jq '.questions[]'`. lint is null on all six, and raisedBy.run is null. q-conversation-retention has every option with sources [] and count 0, not marked 'no source' as 5.6 requires. q-dr1u-remainder has recommended null. q-house-rules-source defaults to A against a recommendation of B, with no reason. The DR1 union question says '43 unbuilt … (34 blocked, 3 deferred, 5 dropped, 1 rejected)', so option A offers to migrate 6 rows already ruled never.
fix: Run a QUESTION_CRITIC pass by hand now, as a different agent, and record lint on each question. Mark unsourced options 'no source'. Give the DR1 union question a recommendation. Restate its scope as 37 unbuilt increments (34 blocked, 3 deferred), and name the 6 ruled-out rows as staying ruled.

problem: The default for the Codex parity bar quietly weakens Sam's R6 ('just as good'), and the options leave out the obvious answer. Fixed 90% and 80% thresholds cannot tell 'as good' from 'worse' without knowing how far two Claude runs differ from each other. Under 5.5, a call that contradicts a ruling of Sam's should be escalated to him, not given a default.
evidence: R6 says Codex must be 'seamless and just as good … build to the same standard'. Default A accepts Codex finding 90% of Claude's fix-now findings, with 80% agreement between the judges. Option C's objection ('ordinary variation between runs could fail it') is asserted, not measured. Option C's only source is sam-req.
fix: Add option D and make it the default: Codex must fall within the spread of two Claude runs on the same canaries. This costs one extra Claude build of the three canaries, to measure how often two Claude runs agree on findings and judge rulings. Alternatively, keep option A but class the question as blocking with no default, because it softens R6.

section: decisions-for-sam.md vs DESIGN 9.2 vs backlog.json questions[]
problem: The decisions page is written by hand in three places, and the copies already disagree. This repeats the alignment report's failure, where typed-in facts drifted from state. The page also says 'blocks' where the JSON means 'blocks, or rests on a default'.
evidence: decisions-for-sam.md says the house-rules and DR1 union questions each hold one increment, and DESIGN 9.2 says the panel, parity-bar and canary questions hold nothing. The JSON's blastRadius.increments values are 2, 2, 1, 1 and 1, derived from needs or assumptions. Rule 6.1(1) is 'Generated, never edited', and feedback_backlogs_are_json_state_not_docs says the JSON is the source and a page is only a view of it.
fix: Until inc-025 exists, generate decisions-for-sam.md from questions[] with a small committed script. Failing that, stamp it as a hand-written bootstrap view and add a check that its ids, defaults and blocked increments match the JSON. Split blastRadius into 'blocks' (from needs) and 'restsOnDefault' (from assumptions), and print both.

problem: This programme's own requirements have not been verified or proven complete, and their seal cannot be checked. Sam said quality matters above all, 'especially the requirements gathering'. The design proves coverage for every future programme but not for its own brief, and the fix is one cheap run (feedback_dont_defer_obvious_improvements).
evidence: All 120 atoms are status 'proposed', verdict 'unverified', verifiedBy null. Every source has units null, so P1 to P4 never ran. Every sam-req citation carries seal git-blob:0c51d84…, but `git hash-object` on analysis/sam-requirements.md gives 62b7f41…, and `git cat-file -t 0c51d84…` fails, so the seal was typed in. Atoms cite only 31 distinct lines of sam-requirements.md. Line 13 (two-pass distillation), the R6 executor-profile paragraph (lines 72-82) and R4 lines 127-129 are never cited from that source. inc-001 to inc-009 are built on unverified atoms.
fix: Before inc-001, run one registered verification by hand. A different agent walks sam-requirements.md sentence by sentence and records either the atom that cites each sentence or why it was dismissed, and a second agent checks every dismissal. Reseal from `git hash-object`. Record the result under distil/ so inc-010 ingests it instead of repeating it.

problem: Nothing checks mechanically that each section stands alone or that the prose is plain English. No task reads the rendered page as a whole; the claim verifier checks one field at a time.
evidence: `report --lint` checks only dashes, question-form headlines, bare ids and duration phrases. decisions-for-sam.md already relies on shorthand that a reader coming to one section alone would not know: 'Judge 3', 'two judges read the review skill as one reviewer per repo', 'the synthesis'.
fix: Add lint rules for sentences over 25 words outside quotes and for abbreviations used without expansion on first use, with a glossary in the profile. Add a COLD_READER task on each render that reads every section on its own and fails any term that section does not define.

problem: Any '?' on an answer line turns it into a tentative answer, so a firm ruling phrased with a rhetorical question gets recorded as tentative. It is caught only if Sam reads the mapping step.
evidence: 6.4 says: Write "?" or "maybe" anywhere in a line to record it as tentative. So 'q-parity-bar: C. Why would we accept less?' would be recorded as tentative.
fix: Treat an answer as tentative only when '?' follows the option letter directly, or when a hedge word appears (maybe, probably, not sure, perhaps). Show 'recorded as tentative because: <token>' in the mapping.

problem: The count of sources behind each option mixes source roles. A repo describing current behaviour, or a constraint, counts the same as a tier-1 requirement source, so 'two against one' can mislead when the one is the authority.
evidence: The option count is simply the number of cited sources. The skeleton shows '2: policy paper; Confluence' against '1: user research session 7'.
fix: Show the count by role ('2 requirement sources, 1 current behaviour') and show each source's precedence tier beside it.

problem: The programme's own backlog fails its writer's role and confidence checks, and its atoms rest on method quotes from the design process, not on requirements. Through show --brief, those recipes reach every build task as requirement evidence.
evidence: sam-req is the only requirement-role source. 92 of 120 atoms cite no requirement-role source, and 64 cite only constraint or current-behaviour sources (req-001..009, 011..015, 018, 022, 023, 025, 026, 028..035, 038, 055..058, 061, 064, 066, 067, 071..077, 079, 082, 085..087, 090..100, 102, 106, 110, 111, 113). 27 are 'stated' with no requirement-role source (for example req-016, which cites judge-1 only). d-001 has appliesTo [] and decidedBy panel with no registered run. Quotes are method: req-008 'Base the one writer on tim parity ingest + set.js + io.js + schema.js', req-005 'cherry-pick the workareas/shared/dr1-parity-union/ ... paths only', req-050 'a committed tools/codex/run-stage.sh wrapper', req-016 'Add --op-id idempotency', req-054 'Add a tim test asserting...', req-002 'canonical pwd -P path'. 4.2 says show --brief carries 'sources and quotes' to every build task.
fix: Add one Sam-ruled decision per design choice, with appliesTo naming its atoms, or re-source atoms to sam-req and mark the rest inferred and adopted by a named decision. Replace every method quote with the need it serves. Make check --strict over design/backlog.json part of inc-007's acceptance, passing before inc-010.

problem: Acceptance is not independent of the plan. Plans are read by 'every later stage', acceptance inputs are unspecified, and an e2e criterion becomes met when the suite is green. The only link from a criterion to a test is the plan's acceptanceMap.
evidence: 3.1: build/plans/<id>.md is read by 'every later stage'. 8.1: upstream.json is 'accepted outputs of earlier stages this task needs', with no per-stage list. 1609: needs-e2e marks 'become met when its run is green'. About 110 of 125 criteria are e2e, so req-067 ac-1 ('a plan whose proofs pass but whose change misses one criterion') cannot fail for them.
fix: Acceptance inputs are brief.json, manifest diffs, ladder and E2E logs, and per-test results. stage prepare never copies the plan or plan output into an acceptance task, and stage audit checks it. Stage 25 records results per test. Post-E2E acceptance must map each e2e criterion to a named passing test it has read and judged to exercise the criterion, without using acceptanceMap. With no such test, the criterion is not-met.

problem: Review, verify and judge tasks are not specified to receive the requirement plus the plan, and the live personas' ticket.md input has no mapping in the seam.
evidence: FILE_REVIEWER.md:50 'the ticket AC', :82 'Read ticket.md for AC and intent', :179 'Correctness vs the AC in ticket.md'. CONSISTENCY_REVIEWER.md:16 'ticket.md # READ: change intent and AC'. The 8.5 seam rows cover inputs, diff, writing findings, commit and refresh only. No stage states that it gets the plan, so the judge cannot tell a deliberate deferral (plan Out of scope) from a fix-now.
fix: Add a per-stage input matrix enforced by stage prepare: plan-audit, review-*, consistency, verify, judge and fix get brief.json and the plan; acceptance gets the brief only. Add a seam row: ticket.md becomes input/brief.json (acceptance, decisions, invariants) plus input/upstream/plan.md (approach, decisions, out of scope).

problem: Ids do not survive rulings. Only groups with unchanged members are kept. Re-combine matches by content. Solo keys embed the atom key, which changes when a variant supersedes the atom.
evidence: 5.7: 'keeps every group whose members are unchanged'. 4.4: 'match previous items by stable content'. Solo key is solo--<atom key>, and variant req-041 has a different key from req-040. The three blocked rows that rulings will hit (inc-016, inc-031, inc-039) are all solo. 3.9 gives no status for a solo whose member is superseded, because dropped covers only parked or rejected members.
fix: Resolve each member through supersededBy to its root. Key solo increments as solo--<root atom key> and match groups by the set of member roots, with ingest carrying keys forward whatever the combiner writes. Add a test that rules a variant onto a solo member and onto a combined member, and asserts both ids are unchanged.

section: DESIGN 4.3 refusals, 3.4 statement freeze, 3.9, 11.1; backlog as-bootstrap-unverified, q-dr1u-remainder
problem: The writer cannot handle a ruling or verifier correction that touches built work, and the design gives three conflicting stories for it.
evidence: q-dr1u-remainder option C has effect reject req-005, a member of inc-002, which is built second, while ingest refuses to strike started or ruled items. as-bootstrap-unverified says a corrected atom 're-opens that increment'. 11.1 says it 're-opens as discovered work'. 3.9 has no done-to-todo transition. statement is frozen 'at first ingest', but this programme's atoms are ingested proposed by migrate --from design, so inc-010 cannot correct a statement.
fix: tim backlog rule refuses an effect on a member of a started or done increment unless the decision carries reopens:true. That creates a variant atom and a follow-up solo increment depending on the done one, and leaves doneBy untouched. Freeze statement at first adopted ingest, not at migrate. Align the as-bootstrap-unverified text with 11.1.

section: backlog.json questions; DESIGN 3.6, 5.6 lint; decisions-for-sam Q1, Q2
problem: Some options differ in behaviour but have identical effects, so the backlog cannot re-derive which option was ruled and acceptance never checks it. The house-rules default also contradicts its stated consequence.
evidence: q-conversation-retention: A (quotes local only) and B (quotes tracked) both clear-need req-091, and req-091's acceptance says nothing about quote retention. q-house-rules-source: B and C both clear-need req-046. The house-rules default A has effect reject req-046, which drops inc-016, yet decisions-for-sam and 9.2 say 'inc-016 stays blocked'.
fix: Every behaviour-changing option supersedes to variant atoms whose acceptance encodes the option (for example 'the tracked backlog holds no conversational quote'). question lint refuses identical effects across options of a blocking or must-answer question. Correct the house-rules default effect so it matches its text.

section: backlog.json assumptions, deviations; DESIGN 3.14, 3.12 recipe lint, req-021, req-024
problem: Executor and build-mode detail is already in backlog.json as prose. Only keys are refused, and the lint covers only acceptance and statement.
evidence: as-judge-on-codex: 'In the codex preset the judge and acceptance run on Codex'. dv-bootstrap-by-hand: 'built by hand in the main session, not by the build workflow'. as-house-rules-by-path: 'both executors read ... Sam's memory files by path'. 3.14 refuses keys by name, and req-021 lints only acceptance and statement.
fix: Move as-judge-on-codex to presets.json and dv-bootstrap-by-hand to run.json or the journal and handover. Recast house rules neutrally. Extend check's recipe and executor lint to every prose field (assumptions, deviations, invariants, direction, outcome, why, combination.why, statusNote, question text) with an executor vocabulary (Claude, Codex, preset, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, sandbox, main session, by hand). Extend req-024: the backlog contains no executor vocabulary.

problem: One deviation switches off the recipe lint for the whole programme by allowing file paths in acceptance.
evidence: dv-tooling-commands: 'Acceptance may name the pipeline's own commands, skills, workflows and file paths.' 3.12 allows an override 'only by a decision that says a route or a document shape is contract'. inv-no-recipe says 'no files, commands, steps'.
fix: Narrow the deviation to an enumerated interface contract (tim backlog verbs and flags, documented exit codes, skill trigger phrases, stop reasons) and drive the lint allow-list from it. File paths stay refused.

section: DESIGN Principle 1, 3.3 Repo, 3.14; backlog.json repos.workspace, inv-no-recipe
problem: The backlog carries ladders, commands and file globs, which contradicts Principle 1 and the programme's own invariant, so the lint's rule is ambiguous.
evidence: Principle 1: 'The v2 schema refuses file lists, commands, ladders, skill names and executor fields by name.' The header has repos.workspace.ladder (format:check, lint, test, script tools/backlog/self-test.sh, which does not exist yet) and generated[] globs. inv-no-recipe: 'no files, commands'.
fix: Preferred: move ladder, generated and knowledge to the registry entry or build/repos.json, because they describe repos, not requirements. Otherwise amend Principle 1 and inv-no-recipe to exempt repo-level definition-of-done rungs explicitly, and exempt only that path in the lint.

problem: The programme's combining was justified by implementation components, and nothing fences what the combiner may read.
evidence: combination.why: inc-006 'same lock, hash check and validation'; inc-014 'one task-folder contract'; inc-015 'One fake-Codex run'; inc-017 'One zero-model fixture run'; inc-021 'All six are inputs to the done gate' (acceptance, ladder, baseline, secrets, SonarCloud and E2E grouped by one component); inc-022 'One lifecycle stage table'. cr-same-repo-set is vacuous because every increment's repos are [workspace]. 5.7 does not say what COMBINER may read, and mid-build it could read build/plans or DESIGN.
fix: COMBINER reads only atoms, ledgers and candidates --combine output. combination.why must cite candidate signal ids. COMBINE_VERIFIER fails groups justified by a shared implementation component. Lint combination prose. Re-combine the programme, re-examining inc-021 for attributability.

problem: Discovered atoms are born adopted without passing the recipe-smell verifier, and they carry file and line coordinates.
evidence: The discovered[] schema includes source {finding, file, line}. Each item is 'born adopted ... verified by the judge task'. The judge is not REQUIREMENT_VERIFIER and does not run the recipe rubric (5.4).
fix: Born proposed. The record stage runs a separate REQUIREMENT_VERIFIER task plus the recipe lint before adoption. file and line go to build/state.json and the journal, never into atom sources.

section: DESIGN 7.5 ('A repo the plan adds to the surface is allowed'), 7.4 stage order
problem: The plan can widen an increment's repos after the branch, baseline, sync, ladder-facts and routing stages have run on the old surface, and it is undefined whether the plan (the recipe) writes the requirement's surface.
evidence: Stages 3 to 7 (Branch, Baseline, Sync, Ladder facts, Routing) run before stage 8 (Plan), on the backlog surface. 7.5 lets the plan add a repo with a reason. A plan-added repo has no branch, no baseline and no sync, and backlog surface.repos, P11 and the merge order go stale.
fix: A plan that adds a repo returns surfaceChange. The increment is held surface-changed, a discover or rule write updates the member atom's surface.repos with the reason, and the retry starts from stage 3. The plan's file list never writes the backlog.

problem: The destination for migrated legacy recipe fields is undefined, and if they reach the planner they become a stale pre-written recipe.
evidence: req-085: 'with recipe fields moved to plan notes'. No 'plan notes' artefact exists in 3.1 or 10.
fix: Migration writes legacy recipe fields to an existing-backlog source (distil/sources/<legacy-id>/units.json, role current-behaviour). They can be cited, and they never enter brief.json or standards.json. Reword req-085.

problem: The design's own HOW (stage folders, receipts, git mv lineage, stage numbering) has no sanctioned route to this programme's JIT planners. They will reinvent it or pick it up from the method quotes in citations.
evidence: knowledge lists CLAUDE.md, tim/CLAUDE.md, tim/README.md, docs/agent-skills.md, docs/git-conventions.md and AUDITOR.md. DESIGN.md is neither listed nor a registered source.
fix: Add workareas/shared/requirements-pipeline/design/DESIGN.md to repos.workspace.knowledge as the header-level how channel, keep rows requirement-only, and strip the method quotes (see the first blocker).

problem: The diagram and a source quote say the plan audit does not read the plan, but 7.5 says it reads both.
evidence: Line 188: 'PLAN-AUDIT . a different task reads the backlog row, not the plan'. req-060 quotes judge-1: 'reads the row, not the plan'. 7.5: 'reads the backlog row ... and the plan'.
fix: Reword both to 'derives the requirement from the row, never from the plan's restatement of it'.

problem: Option A's effects omit the req-044 supersede that the decision and the ruling text apply.
evidence: 3.6 option A effects: supersede req-040 by req-041, reject req-042. 3.7 and the 'When Sam rules A' text also supersede req-044 by req-045.
fix: Add {op: supersede, target: req-044, by: req-045} to option A and the matching variant to option B.

problem: A solo increment's outcome is a stored copy of the frozen statement, and the prose phase can rewrite it, so it drifts from the statement.
evidence: Example 1 and backlog inc-003, inc-010 and inc-013 carry the statement's MUST text as outcome. 4.1 lists increment outcome as a prose slot, while 3.12 says 'Nothing is copied'.
fix: Render a solo increment's outcome from its member at read time without storing it, or exclude solo outcomes from COPY_EDITOR.

problem: Code citations from consistency-anchor or constraint sources reach the planner through brief.json and act as an exemplar slot under another name.
evidence: 3.4 ref example: 'frontend:src/.../schema.js:12-30'. show --brief includes sources and quotes. 0.3 claims the path-shaped exemplar leak is removed.
fix: show --brief labels non-requirement citations 'evidence of current behaviour, not a design to copy'. The plan audit objects when the plan adopts a cited file as a template without a stated decision.

section: 7.12, 4.6 pin-tools.sh, 8.2, 9.2 'Owed to Sam', decisions-for-sam 'Owed to you'
problem: With toolPin: launch-commit, prompt.md points watchers at bash tools inside workareas/clones/pipeline-pin/tools/. The allowlist covers only tools/** and scripts/** at the workspace root, so every pinned tool call prompts in a headless agent, and agents cannot add an allow rule because guard-edits blocks settings.json. The only other option, running the root copy while the increment edits it, is denied by guard-bash check 2 ('differs from HEAD'). The design's statement 'No allow rule needs adding' is therefore false.
evidence: settings.json allow entries Bash(~/git/defra/trade-imports-workspace/tools/**) and scripts/** only; guard-bash.sh:106-129; FA:73-76 ('the permission allowlist names tools/** at the root path only'); DESIGN 7.12 step 4; DESIGN 9.2.
fix: Pin only tim, through the allowlisted npm --prefix form, plus the briefs and profiles as files. Then either Sam adds Bash(~/git/defra/trade-imports-workspace/workareas/clones/pipeline-pin/tools/**) and its :* twin, listed under 'Owed to Sam' with the 'no allow rule' claim removed, or a self-hosted increment commits any bash tool it changes before a stage calls it. Add a stage-0 preflight that runs a pinned tool's --check and stops with 'environment' if it would prompt.

section: 4.5 stage accept step 5, 4.2 heads --strict, 4.5 stage manifest, 11.1 step 3
problem: Read-only stages fail when HEAD plus 'git status --porcelain' changes between prepare and accept, and heads --strict fails on dirty-at-start. The design dropped FA's clones mode, so builds share the live workspace checkout, which carries other sessions' untracked files under the tracked workareas/shared/. The workflow also writes its own tracked state (state.json, journal.jsonl, plans/<id>.md, backlog.json) into that same repo mid-increment, and accept step 4 writes before step 5 compares. Every self-hosted increment from inc-025 therefore starts dirty-tree or fails its read-only stages, and systemicHaltAfter then stops the run. The manifest also sends the programme's state files to per-file reviewers, because the workspace repo's generated[] does not exclude them.
evidence: DESIGN 4.5 steps 4-5, 3.1 (state files tracked); design/backlog.json repos.workspace.generated = [tim/package-lock.json, workareas/**/report/*.html]; git status shows 11 untracked entries under workareas/shared/; FA:31-45, 77-79 (clones mode); memory 'repos/ checkouts move mid-session'.
fix:
Scope fingerprints and dirty checks to tracked files (--untracked-files=no) and to the increment's plan and manifest paths. Exclude workareas/shared/

/** from the workspace repo's fingerprint, dirty check and manifest by rule. Bring back FA's clones checkout mode as a run.json knob, and make it the default for self-hosting.

problem: 'git add --chmod=+x' sets only the index mode. The Write tool creates files as 644 and chmod is denied, so the working tree stays 644 and guard-bash denies the script as 'differs from HEAD'.
evidence: memory reference_write_tool_drops_execute_bit.md and reference_new_executables_chmod_and_guard.md (update-index --chmod=+x, commit, then git checkout -- <path>; check 'create mode 100755'); settings.json deny Bash(chmod *).
fix: State the full sequence (add, update-index --chmod=+x, commit, checkout -- <path>) in 4.6 and in inc-001, inc-015, inc-017, inc-021 and inc-024. Make self-test.sh fail if any tools/backlog or tools/codex script is not 100755 at HEAD.

section: 3.3 ladder tool: script, 4.6 run-rung.sh, 7.4 stage 19, backlog.json workspace ladder
problem: The ladder (stage 19) runs before land (stage 22), so a new or edited script rung is uncommitted. Invoked directly, guard check 2 denies it. As a child of run-rung.sh the guard never sees it, and it either fails as 644 (recorded red, not skipped-undefined) or, if run-rung uses 'bash <file>', becomes the write-then-execute laundering the guard exists to stop.
evidence: guard-bash.sh:5-6 (the incident), :106-129; memory feedback_never_bypass_deny_rules; backlog.json ladder rung {dir:'.', tool:'script', name:'tools/backlog/self-test.sh'}.
fix: run-rung.sh refuses uncommitted or modified script rungs (could-not-run:uncommitted). Move the tool self-test behind a named npm script, for example tim test:tools. Drop 'tool: script' from the v2 schema, or limit it to paths the increment cannot touch.

problem: Each per-file Claude task runs stage accept itself, up to 16 at once. Accept writes shared state (state.plan, counts) under a lock that exits 4 after three retries. Agents are told to 'correct the draft' on problems, but a LOCKED exit is not a draft fault. 4.3's 'serialise writes through one watcher' contradicts 8.2.
evidence: DESIGN 8.2 adapter text; 4.3 lock retries then exit 4; 4.5 accept step 4 side effects.
fix: Per-task accept writes only output.json and receipt.json in the task folder. All shared-state side effects move to one 'stage accept --stage <dir> --finalise' call by a single watcher after the fan-out. Agents treat exit 4 as 'rerun unchanged'.

problem: The manifest diffs '<base>...HEAD' with <base> undefined. Under programme delivery (default here), base is main, so each increment's manifest holds every earlier increment's files and state commits, and the audit then demands style and code reviews for all of them. The review cost and agent count grow every increment toward the 850 ceiling.
evidence: DESIGN 4.5 manifest bullet; design/backlog.json delivery {branchStrategy: programme, base: main}.
fix: Define base as the attempt's pinned baseline heads (state.heads from stage 4) per repo, and record it in stage.json so the audit re-derives the same set.

section: 5.10 Word row, 5.2 phases 2-3, 9.2 S6 default A
problem: Word conversion relies on 'unzip -p' plus a sed tag-marking pass. unzip is not allowlisted, and the sed and redirect chain breaks the GUARD RAILS. tim has no zip library and adds only picomatch and acorn, so source acquire cannot do it either. The default distiller canary (plants plus EUDPA-407) needs Word sources.
evidence: journey-builder/references/SOURCE_EXTRACTOR.md:29,125-126; settings.json allow list (no unzip); DESIGN 4.7 dependency list; decisions-for-sam S6 A 'exercises Word, design-board and Jira sources'.
fix: Add a zip library (fflate or jszip) to 4.7 and have 'tim backlog source acquire' convert docx to raw/<id>.txt with paragraph, row and cell markers, tested on a fixture. Or add a committed tools/backlog/docx-to-text.sh to the new-file ledger. Prove it in inc-030.

problem: Codex implement, fix and repair tasks get workspace-write over the whole workspace, and guard-edits never runs for Codex. A Codex task can edit .claude/settings*.json or .claude/hooks/**, and the manifest only lists that as one more file to review. No rule refuses it, so later Claude agents would run under weakened guards.
evidence: DESIGN 8.2 table (workspace-write, cwd the workspace); 8.7 'Codex is fenced by its sandbox, the manifest and tree fingerprints'; guard-edits.sh protects those paths only for Claude tool calls.
fix: stage manifest and accept refuse, as a hold, any change by any task under .claude/settings*.json, .claude/hooks/** or a repo's .git/hooks/**. Limit Codex writable roots to the planned repos (--add-dir) instead of the workspace root.

problem: The parity bar's exact check 'no unread must file' needs each Claude transcript mapped to its task. The workflow script cannot know its run or session id or its transcript directory, and nothing establishes that a transcript records the agent() label. Without a deterministic mapping the exact check cannot be computed.
evidence: DESIGN 8.10 bar 'no unread must file on either side'; 0.4 (scripts have no clock and no file access); memory feedback_no_sonar_cd_in_workflow_agents (transcripts at subagents/workflows/<run>/agent-*.jsonl).
fix: Make the adapter's first instruction 'Read <taskDir>/prompt.md', so each transcript's first Read names the task folder. Run audit-reading from the skill after the Workflow returns, using the transcript directory the result names. Prove it on a two-agent fixture in inc-019.

problem: inc-010 must record verifications from 'a registered run's task'. It is built by hand before inc-014 creates task folders, stage.json and receipts, and before backlog-distil.js exists. There is therefore no task identity the ingest guard can check, and req-081's criterion cannot be met as specified.
evidence: backlog.json req-081 ('every verification names a registered run'); inc-010 depends on inc-007 and inc-009 only; task folders arrive in inc-014 (DESIGN 8.1, 11.3).
fix: Either have inc-008 add 'run task add' ids for verify-record to check, or move inc-010 after inc-014 and run the verifiers through stage prepare and accept from an inline main-session Workflow. Say that the main session spawns them, because subagents cannot call Workflow.

problem: 'npm --prefix … run tim -- … --json' prints npm's '> tim@0.0.0 tim' banner to stdout before the JSON, which breaks one-JSON-line consumers.
evidence: tim/package.json scripts.tim = 'node src/cli.js'.
fix: Use 'npm --prefix … run --silent tim -- …' and test that the pinned form's stdout parses as JSON.

problem: Workflow scripts use 'export const meta' and a top-level return, which default acorn options reject.
evidence: increment-build-loop.js:1925 'return { increments: results }'; FA line 1 'export const meta'.
fix: Parse with sourceType 'module' and allowReturnOutsideFunction true, with a fixture that uses both.

problem: A rung longer than 570 seconds is recorded could-not-run:timeout, and the audit accepts only pass or skipped-undefined. A long mvn verify or full tests-repo suite therefore holds an increment forever, with no route out.
evidence: DESIGN 4.6 run-rung.sh row; 4.5 audit 'Every ladder rung is pass or skipped-undefined'.
fix: Let a rung declare a narrower goal or slices, or turn a timeout into an 'environment' hold with a release command. Measure the backend verify time in inc-021.

section: 8.2 'No agent relays a large JSON array'
problem: Scripts cannot read files, so the fan-out list from stage prepare (80+ rows for 40 files) must be relayed through a Haiku watcher's structured output. A dropped row surfaces only later, as a hold.
evidence: DESIGN 4.5 prepare returns the task list; 0.4 scripts cannot read files.
fix: prepare prints a compact list plus a count and the sha256 of stage.json. The script checks the relayed count and hash before it fans out.

problem: Agents commit without 'sonar analyze --staged', breaking CLAUDE.md banned-action rule 3 with no recorded deviation. 8.7 also claims the PostToolUse push hook fires for every push, but its if: Bash(git push*) never matches the refspec form 'git -C … push'.
evidence: settings.json PostToolUse 'if': 'Bash(git push*)'; FA:125-128 push form; memory reference_sonar_analyze_unavailable.
fix: Add a deviations[] entry and decision to the header ('agents commit without sonar analyze --staged; SonarCloud from PR checks'), and correct the 8.7 push-hook row.

problem: A Codex draft that fails `stage accept` can never be fixed. A Claude task gets three correction tries. `run-stage.sh` runs only tasks that have no output.draft.json, and the Codex watcher runs accept only once, so a rejected Codex draft is skipped forever and never gets a receipt. The increment is then held. The semantic checks (ladder .exit cross-check, manifest, pre-existing without baselineRef, fingerprints) cannot be expressed in --output-schema, so this hits Codex hardest on repair and acceptance stages.
evidence: DESIGN.md:909 'A Claude task corrects its draft and retries, at most three times'; :1913-1918 Claude adapter retries accept; :1929-1933 Codex watcher runs accept once after exit 0/1; :1939 run-stage runs only tasks 'which have no output.draft.json'.
fix: On rejection, accept moves the draft to rejected-<n>.json, writes input/extras/accept-problems-<n>.json and marks the task needs-correction in runner.json. run-stage.sh treats needs-correction as unfinished and resumes the task's own session with the problems, up to three times to match Claude. The watcher loops run-stage then accept. Add a self-test case: a draft that is valid under the schema but fails a semantic check, then a corrected resume.

problem: Codex's implementer, fixer and repairers cannot run the checks that prove their own work. Claude's can. Codex cannot start Chromium for browser rungs or the E2E specs R7 makes mandatory, and cannot reach Docker for Testcontainers, so it cannot run `mvn verify`. Suites longer than the 540-second slice are killed and restarted on resume. So Codex hands unproven integration tests and E2E specs to stage 19, where a blind Codex repair gets 3 attempts across the whole ladder. The parity bar's ladder comparison would measure how much repair budget each side used, not how good the work was.
evidence: codex/implement.md:83-87 (run mvn verify), :123-132 (Chromium refused its Mach port); codex/fix.md:45-53. Testcontainers appears in the pom.xml of animals-backend, plants-backend, address-book and reference-data. DESIGN.md:2017 'The Codex sandbox does not reach Docker'; :1596 repair limited to 3 across the ladder; :1951 540-second deadline.
fix: Add stage 11b, 'implement check': a watcher runs the browser and Docker rungs for the changed files through run-rung.sh. On red, it resumes the same implement task with the log and error-context.md (codex exec resume, or a Claude follow-on), with the same number of rounds for both executors. Re-run the rung in a watcher after every fix, ladder-repair and e2e-repair attempt. Tell both executors' briefs that watchers run browser and Docker rungs, so the comparison is symmetric.

section: 2.2 stage briefs; 10 retire table; 8.3 executor profiles
problem: codex/implement.md and fix.md are moved by git mv to become neutral stage briefs, but they contain Codex-only rules: browser suites are not yours to run, no sandbox bypass, and always emit a final message even if unfinished. The 8.3 profile table carries none of them. If the rules stay in the neutral brief, Claude is told to skip browser suites too, so parity is reached by making Claude worse. If they are removed, Codex loses them and fails at Chromium launch.
evidence: DESIGN.md:220 and :2361-2362 (git mv to stages/); :1985-1992 has only six profile rows; codex/implement.md:123-132, codex/fix.md:50-53, codex/review.md:119-123; increment-build-loop.js:1405-1415 exists because 'the implementor cannot run' browser suites.
fix: Before inc-014, sort every sentence of the three briefs into neutral (stays in the stage brief), Codex-only (moves to executors/codex.md) or Claude-only (moves to executors/claude.md), with the table recorded in the plan. Add a contract test that fails if a neutral brief mentions sandbox, Codex, GUARD RAILS or the Write tool.

problem: Codex writing tasks get rules only for the files the plan names. Claude gets the matching .claude/rules natively for any file it reads, including tests-repo specs, Java records and copy files the plan never named. Stage 13 re-routes changed files only for the reviewers, after Codex has already written those files without their rules. Fix, ladder-repair and ci-fix tasks, which routinely touch unplanned files, have the same gap.
evidence: DESIGN.md:1587 'Routing (planned files) → implement standards.json'; :2084-2085; rules-probe conclusion 1; codex/implement.md:97-103, which requires editing the preceding page's spec even though no plan names it.
fix: Every writing task's standards.json is the union of the planned-file routing and the repo-level routing (stage 7, tim backlog rules --repo-level) for every repo in the surface. Stage 13 records rulesGap[]: changed files whose rules were missing from the writing task's list. The stage audit fails on a non-empty gap for either executor.

section: 8.2 Codex adapter and slices; 7.7 codexParallel; 7.4 stage 14
problem: The watcher's 12-call limit does not grow with the number of tasks. A 30-file R7 increment is 61 Codex review tasks at 4 in parallel, about 9 to 14 calls. The design never says what happens when the watcher reaches 12 with run-stage still returning 75. The slice deadline is per call, so a task that starts late still uses one of its 5 slices. Claude's 'missing receipt retries once' has no Codex equivalent.
evidence: DESIGN.md:1931 'at most 12 calls in all'; :1951-1953; :1726 codexParallel 4; :1728 reviewCap null; :1922 Claude concurrency 16; :1591 a missing receipt retries once.
fix: Loop while runner.json shows progress, stop after two calls in a row with none, and report a named stop, codex-stalled. Count slices by each task's own wall-clock time. Start no new task in the last 60 seconds of a call. Give each failed task one fresh start. Allow codexParallel per sandbox mode, for example 8 for read-only and 2 for write.

problem: Nothing stops two run-stage.sh processes from running on the same stage folder. A Haiku watcher that gets the timeout wrong has its call moved to the background, and a watcher that dies (agent() returns null) may leave its child running. The next call, or a relaunch, then starts a second codex exec for the same task. For implement and fix, that means two Codex sessions editing one working tree.
evidence: DESIGN.md:1937-1969 describes no lock; :873 locks cover only tim's canonical files; increment-build-loop.js:746-759 documents calls moved to the background.
fix: run-stage.sh takes an exclusive `mkdir <stageDir>/.run.lock` holding {pid, startedAt}. A live lock exits 3 ('already running'); a stale lock is broken with a note. The runner records each task's child pid and refuses to start a task whose pid is still alive. Add both cases to the self-test.

problem: Every codex exec inherits ~/.codex/config.toml: the model, personality and notify program; MCP servers idea (unreachable) and node_repl (120-second startup timeout); and the browser and computer-use plugins. So each slice pays MCP startup time, and MCP tools run outside the read-only sandbox. The model and CLI version are never recorded, so the parity comparison cannot detect a config change between the two runs.
evidence: ~/.codex/config.toml:3-6 (notify, model gpt-6-astra, model_reasoning_effort), :99-128 (mcp_servers), :171-181 (browser and computer-use plugins); DESIGN.md:1996 uses the 'CLI's configured default'; receipt at :1900-1903 records only tier.
fix: Run Codex with a pipeline-owned CODEX_HOME: auth.json symlinked, a minimal committed config.toml with no MCP servers, plugins or notify, and an explicit model. Record codex --version and the model from the exec header in runner.json and the receipt. compare fails on a mismatch, and --check prints the effective configuration.

problem: Codex-orchestrated mode stalls. A proof-owed hold withholds every dependent increment, so a Codex batch builds one increment per dependency chain and then stops at none-buildable. Browser ladder rungs are left out of the owed set and go ladder-red instead. The orchestrating session's sandbox is never named, yet it must push, commit state, call GitHub and Jira, and start nested codex exec processes. 'Through run-stage.sh or directly' lets tasks run in the orchestrator's own context, which breaks the different-task rule. And its pushes bypass the hooks that 0.3 relies on.
evidence: DESIGN.md:2194 'through tools/codex/run-stage.sh or directly'; :2204 proof-owed; :537-541 buildability requires dependsOn done and no hold; :78 'Lifecycle stays in Claude watcher agents … every per-call hook sees every push'.
fix: Require a full-access orchestrating session, stated in the handover and verified by --check. Remove 'or directly'. Replace the proof-owed hold with a per-criterion owed mark: the increment is landed, not done, but satisfies dependsOn for build ordering. Add browser ladder rungs to the owed set. State which 0.3 guarantees this mode gives up, and add a committed pre-push check.

problem: The only way offered to unblock Codex-orchestrated builds is to edit `delivery.crossRepoE2e` in backlog.json through a ruling. That is an executor-driven backlog edit, which R5 forbids, and req-024's hash check would not catch it because the edit goes through rule, not run bind.
evidence: decisions-for-sam.md:147-148; DESIGN.md:750 classes delivery as a backlog field; :1610.
fix: Move where the integration proof may come from into build/run.json as quality.integrationProofSource: local | ci | either. Keep delivery about branches, PRs and merges only. Extend req-024's acceptance to cover switching into Codex-orchestrated mode.

problem: The exact bar 'no unread must file' is judged by parsing Codex's plain-text log.txt, appended across slices. Partial sed reads, cat, rg -l and loops will produce both false misses and false hits, while Claude's side is structured JSON. So how accurate the parser is decides whether Codex is called equal.
evidence: DESIGN.md:2168 'read commands in Codex logs'; :2176 the bar must hold exactly; :1949 session id taken by grepping a log line; req-084.
fix: Run codex exec --json and write events.jsonl. Take the session id from the structured thread.started event. The audit counts a file as read only when command output covers its full line range, or covers it cumulatively. Apply the same rule to Claude Read calls with offset and limit. Add fixture tests for sed ranges, cat, rg -l and a loop.

problem: Nothing proves the zod source and the Codex-strict export accept the same drafts. Codex must emit null for optional keys. If zod uses .optional() rather than .nullish(), every Codex draft fails accept, every time, while Claude drafts that omit the key pass. zod refinements are invisible in the exported schema, so only Claude learns about them, from accept's messages.
evidence: DESIGN.md:920 and :1880 'optional values nullable'; :1990 null for anything that does not apply; increment-build-loop.js:698 relay already works around this mismatch ('omit line where Codex returned null').
fix: Add a contract test per stage schema: a document valid under the export with every nullable field null must pass zod, and the reverse after normalisation. Forbid .refine in stage schemas, or list each refinement in the neutral stage brief.

problem: FILE_REVIEWER tells the reviewer the per-PR bundle is the single source and not to read individual docs/best-practices files. That contradicts standards.json's 'must' list of individual files, and the seam table has no row for it. A Codex reviewer that obeys the persona reads nothing, while Claude still has its rules injected.
evidence: review/references/FILE_REVIEWER.md:71-81; DESIGN.md:2048-2054.
fix: Add a seam row: best-practice source → the 'must' files in input/standards.json, which replace the per-PR bundle.

problem: Claude agents receive the memory index at start, which holds about a dozen code rules beyond the four house rules. Codex sees them only if it reads the index, and the design never marks the index as 'must'.
evidence: DESIGN.md:90 (0.4); :2069 memory listed without a must class.
fix: Put the memory index in every writing and reviewing task's 'must' list for both executors, and have the reading audit check it.

problem: Killing by process group may leave grandchildren running: sandboxed tool commands such as mvn, vitest workers and Testcontainers containers can outlive the slice and hold ports and target/ locks when the resumed session re-runs the suite.
evidence: DESIGN.md:1952 'stops every child it started, by process group'.
fix: Kill the whole descendant tree, walking pgrep -P recursively. Add a fake-codex self-test that spawns a grandchild in a new process group.

problem: The self-test checks the flags of exec --help but not those of exec resume, and the runner depends on resume accepting -o, --output-schema and -s before the subcommand.
evidence: DESIGN.md:1969; increment-build-loop.js:767-768.
fix: Also check `codex exec resume --help`, and run one real no-op resume under --check.
